summary: A 1939-40 stone tower with a wooden cab on the Virginia-West Virginia line, built by WWI veterans and CCC crews; restored 2001-2003, hiked to today, with the cab interior not open at a 2018 visit.

facts.design: About 20 ft stone base with a wooden 14x14 ft cab and catwalk; the only stone lookout in Virginia

access.note: Trail and tower exterior open to hikers; the cab interior was not open to visitors at the May 2018 NHLR visit, and the visitor wished it could be opened

visit.trail_note: 2.5-mile out-and-back trail, about 1.5 to 2.5 hours, about 643 ft of elevation change; trailhead about 30 minutes west of Harrisonburg by car

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (George Washington National Forest, Dry River Ranger District)

events.note: Construction started in 1939 by World War I veterans under John Moffett; NHLR's Built field gives 1939, while its description says the tower was completed in 1940 by CCC Camp #2 crews
Gerald Fawley moved from a tree platform into the finished stone tower for the 1940 fire season and stayed three more seasons
Forest Service memo proposed declaring the forest's fire towers surplus and removing them, except Elliott Knob and Reddish Knob; a district ranger asked to keep High Knob
Registered January 27, 1994 on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 76 (VA 1)
NHLR says restored in 2003; trail guide says restored from 2001 to 2003

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR Built field gives 1939, which matches the start of construction. Its own description and the Friends of Shenandoah Mountain history say the tower was finished in 1940. The record keeps 1939 as the build start and the story gives both dates.
NHLR says the tower was restored in 2003. The Visit Harrisonburg trail guide says it was restored from 2001 to 2003. Both are reported; the restoration is treated as spanning those years.

notes_for_editor: Do not use fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/high-knob-tower for this record: that page describes the High Knob Tower in the Clinch Ranger District (Wise County, VA), a different tower with a 2014 rebuild. The GWNF High Knob is in Rockingham County, VA. Staffing is recorded as unknown because the sources read do not say when the tower last had a lookout. Interior access is recorded as restricted based on the 2018 NHLR visit comment, which is not an official closure notice; a current check with the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests is advised. Trail details come from the Visit Harrisonburg guide (2025 PDF).
